messages:
simone: Heads-up — I opened a small terraform change to add a separate nodepool for short/burst GPU jobs (mostly <30m). Want to get input on instance types, taints/tolerations, and how we wire secrets/IRSA for sidecar access. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1423

alex c: Nice. Quick skim — are we doing this as SPOT/Preemptible only, or mixed? my concern is long-running checkpoints getting killed.

simone: Plan was SPOT-only for cost; workloads are short inference batches. We’ll rely on retry logic in job controller. But we can add fallback to on-demand if eviction rate > X. open to suggestions.

maddy: If SPOT-only, recommend a separate nodepool label + taint so nothing else lands there. Example k8s taint: `dedicated=burst:NoSchedule` and pod toleration in job spec. Keep autoscaler min size small (0 or 1) and max moderate.

simone: Yep added: `labels = { "nodepool-type" = "burst-gpu" }` and taint via kubelet_extra_args in TF. snippet in PR: ```hcl
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "burst_gpu" {
  cluster_name    = var.cluster
  node_group_name = "burst-gpu"
  instance_types  = ["g5.xlarge", "g4dn.xlarge"]
  capacity_type   = "SPOT"
  desired_size    = 0
  min_size        = 0
  max_size        = 6
  labels = {"workload" = "short-infer"}
  taints = ["dedicated=burst:NoSchedule"]
}
```

rajiv: Looks reasonable. For AWS EKS, also set `launch_template` with `capacity_reservation_specification` if we ever want persistent capacity for a subset of nodes. But that’s more on-demand. For SPOT, consider `allocation_strategy = "capacityOptimized"`.

alex c: Also ensure cluster-autoscaler sees the nodegroup: tag like `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled` and `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/<cluster-name>=owned`. Otherwise scaling won't trigger reliably.

maddy: Secret wiring: pods need access to S3 presign and KMS decrypt for model artifacts. Use IRSA service account annotation so we don't have to give node role broad permissions. In TF add `aws_iam_role` and `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment` for the service account.

simone: Good call. I added an IAM role and updated `kubernetes_service_account` resource with `annotations = {"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.burst_pod_role.arn }`. Should we store model keys in Secrets Manager or SSM?

rajiv: Secrets Manager is fine. For short-lived jobs we can issue short-term credentials and mount as env vars via projected token. Avoid baking credentials on node role.

alex c: One more operational note: set node-group scaling cooldowns lower than normal since jobs are short — and use `graceful_termination` hooks in job controller so we can checkpoint small state. Also add a stackdriver/cloudwatch alert for >15% eviction rate in 15m.

infra-bot: deploybot: terraform plan for `aws_eks_node_group.burst_gpu` succeeded in staging — plan id `plan-20260317-8a3f`.

maddy: Can someone review the PR specifically for: 1) taint/toleration correctness, 2) autoscaler tags, 3) IRSA wiring? I can pair on the IAM bits.

simone: @maddy @alex c tagging you both. I'm going to run a small synthetic load on staging once merged. If eviction hits >25% we'll flip to mixed instance types (add one on-demand `g5.xlarge`).

alex c: I can review the autoscaler and toleration parts this afternoon. If you want a quick safety, add a `nodeSelector` on the job too so nothing else accidentally lands there.

simone: Added nodeSelector in job template. Thanks all — I'll wait for reviews and then merge. :thumbsup:
